p30ecd6ee97.reason: gravestone inscription (a person's name and dates) in a Lviv cemetery; not a mappable place sign

p63f3d6aaa3.reason: gravestones in a Lviv cemetery (family name КОНОПАДА); personal names, not a mappable place sign

p2e2d2d4d97.notes: Kharkiv: black stone memorial plaque explaining the street name (вулиця Квітки-Основ'яненка), shot upward at an angle. Apostrophes are typographic (’) on the plaque; 'р.р.' is in smaller letters. A small torn sticker sits at the lower left of the plaque.

pad16b4be66.notes: Kyiv ghost-bike memorial (OSM memorial=ghost_bike). Title letters are cut-out stencil letters in a steel plate, so the background shows through and contrast is low; the three small lines below are engraved and small.

c134354822.notes: Luhansk Oblast, end-of-settlement sign (red diagonal bar across the name, crossing the С and Ь), small in the frame and shot through a car window; car mirror at bottom left. Below it: 24 t weight-limit and axle-load signs, with a partly painted-over plate.

c134261670.notes: Starobilsk, Luhansk Oblast. Fallen blue direction board leaning on a kerb, slightly bent. Left arrow with route H-26 for the upper three, right arrow with H-26 for the lower three. Weeds partly cover the Ь of БІЛОВОДСЬК and the bottom of МІЛОВЕ. Apostrophe in КУП’ЯНСЬК is a typographic ’.

c173380275.notes: Khmelnytskyi Oblast, white village-entry sign, near-frontal. Distractors: speed-camera and service pictogram signs with '3км', a military billboard at left.

c134261484.notes: Luhansk Oblast. Small settlement sign seen through a car windscreen (mirror and dashboard frame the view). The sign is in Russian ('пгт.', 'Донецкий'), not Ukrainian (смт Донецький), so the map query uses the Ukrainian form.

c181869341.reason: two overlapping old plates: the end of 'ФАБРИЧНА…' is hidden behind a detached, rusted vertical plate whose letters (…Капітана/Капитана Семенюка) are too corroded to transcribe without guessing

c53184556.notes: Brovary, Kyiv Oblast. Rusty stencilled Soviet-era street plate in Russian with a separate house-number plate 8; the 'ул.' is faint. The street has since been renamed вулиця Степана Бандери (Stepana Bandery), so a current map may only have the new name. Angled shot.

c118500104.reason: the subject is the Blue Palace building; its only signs are small bank/ATM panels ('УКРСОЦБАНК', 'БАНКОМАТ'), no name board for the building

c180853850.notes: Village entry sign with a fluorescent yellow-green border; Ukrainian and Latin transliteration. A small scratch/sticker after the final А is not a letter; sunlight glare on the right half.

c180883692.notes: Vinnytsia Oblast. White village entry sign, weathered and slightly soft (shot through a car window). Priority-road sign at left is a distractor.

c53263898.notes: Horlivka (2011). Black lightbox over the corner door of a bookshop; panoramic stitch. Distractors at right: 'МИР ФОТО на документы' and 'КСЕРО КОПИЯ' signs (Russian), graffiti 'MO'.

c54886300.reason: wide street scene; the shop signs ('ЭЛИТНАЯ МЕБЕЛЬ', 'ГАСТРОНОМ') are small and partly blocked by a pole and tree, and the rest is advertising

c103653907.notes: Kyiv. Lightbox corner plate with the new name and the former name in brackets, house number 66 on the side panels. A CCTV camera sits on top.

c133611079.notes: Kyiv (Pechersk). Direction plate with a green left arrow, slightly out of focus. Below it an insurance advert panel ('ІНГО УКРАЇНА', 'ІНГО життя', '390-57-47, вул. ЦИТАДЕЛЬНА, 3, 3-й пов.') is a distractor/advert.

c193850137.notes: Kharkiv. Old blue enamel plate under a corrugated roof. The avenue was renamed проспект Любові Малої in 2015, so a current map may only have the new name.

c3874935.notes: Kherson. Old Russian-language enamel lane plate (Ukrainian form: Санаторний провулок) with a dark rusted house-number plate 15 below.

c76802044.notes: Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv Oblast. Modern blue-and-white address plate with house number 21 in the white panel, serif lettering, frontal.
